primary_claim: AntiPaSTO, a gradient-optimized self-supervised steering method trained only on two contrastive words, achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2 on Gemma-3-1B for honesty steering on out-of-distribution moral dilemmas, versus 4.5 for prompting and 0.0 for arithmetic mean-difference steering (ActAdd/RepEng).
stated_future_work: Extend the method to cover the KV cache rather than only next-token residual-stream planning, which may help steering persist over longer generations and extend to reasoning models and chain of thought
limitations_stated: No supervised ceiling exists for this task, since computing one would require training on the evaluation preference labels
Seed variance is high (std of about 5 to 7 F1 points), so initialization determines convergence to a useful minimum
No in-distribution evaluation exists, so it cannot be measured whether OOD gains come at the cost of in-distribution degradation
Multi-axis results have high variance on axes with small evaluation pools, and the 'courageous' value axis is an outright failure
The suppression-bypass finding (steering working where prompting triggers refusal) is preliminary and the author states he does not fully trust it
quote: AntiPaSTO on Gemma 3 1B achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2, beating the prompting baseline of 4.5.
